summary: Implemented a policy-local decoder that maps named references from the parser's entity table and decimal or hexadecimal numeric references to characters, using the decoded value only for the URI scheme comparison. Bounded local test: hex, decimal, uppercase-hex, named-colon, named-tab, named-newline and numeric-control variants of javascript: and file: lost the URI attribute; plain allowed http(s), mailto, relative, query-ampersand and custom-protocol values kept their exact serialized bytes. The original local suite passed (234 tests), and 16 new focused checks passed (250 total, 2 expected failures). A nested double-encoded reference stayed unchanged, consistent with single-pass browser resolution. Evidence strength: direct local causal result with byte-level controls. Limitation: only link attributes and semicolon-terminated references were exercised; the official evaluator was not run.
next_hint: Apply the same check to every URI-valued attribute class and to malformed, out-of-range, double-encoded and semicolon-less references. Distinguish a shared policy repair from a link-only special case, and look for a reference form the decoder still misses.
